title: Other Common PHP Extensions
keywords: dates, mathematics, json, and built-in extensions
learning_outcomes: Explain what other common php extensions contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: curl.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Dates, numeric functions, JSON, and extensions convert data between representations. Be deliberate about time zones, encoding errors, precision, required extensions, and failure conditions. In this lesson, focus on curl; then compare it with openssl. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use other common php extensions when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Dates, numeric functions, JSON, and extensions convert data between representations. Be deliberate about time zones, encoding errors, precision, required extensions, and failure conditions. For other common php extensions, begin with curl. Also distinguish openssl; mbstring; fileinfo. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Other Common PHP Extensions
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$sql = "SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE category = :category";
$params = [":category" => "books"];
echo str_contains($sql, ":category") && isset($params[":category"]) ? "named placeholder ready" : "check binding";

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for other common php extensions from top to bottom. Start by identifying curl, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
